theme: Long-term rent indices: Zillow ZORI/ZHVI downloaders, Apartment List, Redfin data center, Realtor.com, HUD Fair Market Rents, Census ACS rent, CoStar-like
queries_run: gh search repos "zillow research data" --sort stars
gh search repos "apartment list rent estimates" --sort stars
gh search repos "HUD fair market rent" --sort stars
gh search repos "redfin data center" --sort stars
gh search repos "ZORI OR ZHVI" --sort updated
gh search repos "apartment list rent" --sort stars

candidates.name: redfin-market-pulse
candidates.what_it_holds: Automated ETL pipeline (README.md, DAY1_GETTING_STARTED.md, .gitignore-'d data dir) that pulls U.S. real estate market data from Redfin's public 'Data Center' TSV/CSV downloads (median sale price, days on market, inventory by metro/zip). No data committed to the repo itself (data dir gitignored) -- it is a scheduled puller, not a static mirror. Small, 0 stars, very new (Apr 2026).
candidates.why_useful: Redfin Data Center covers home-price/inventory series that move with the same regional housing-cost dynamics that feed into long-term-rental supply (hosts converting owned units to STR); a working, documented client for the Redfin bulk downloads saves us from re-writing the pull ourselves, though we'd still need to run it to get an actual point-in-time file.
candidates.time_coverage: current + historical Redfin Data Center vintages (puller does not itself commit history)
candidates.size_hint: no data committed; pulls Redfin's public TSVs directly

candidates.name: ETL-Housing-Pipeline
candidates.what_it_holds: Dockerized ETL + REST API repo (Dockerfile, README) that combines Zillow (ZHVI/ZORI-style), HUD Fair Market Rent, and Census ACS median household income data by zip code into a housing-affordability index. Contents check shows only Dockerfile/README/.gitignore at top level -- no committed CSVs, everything pulled live from the three sources at run time.
candidates.why_useful: A single working reference implementation for joining Zillow + HUD FMR + ACS by zip code; useful as a recipe/pipeline for reconstructing a long-run local rent-cost benchmark rather than as a data source itself.
candidates.time_coverage: current vintage of each source API at pipeline run time
candidates.size_hint: no data committed; Docker ETL job

candidates.name: Housing-Market-Data-Analysis (HUD API + Census ACS)
candidates.what_it_holds: Single Jupyter notebook ('Mathew Scaria - Parts1-3.ipynb', ~95KB) that calls the HUD Fair Market Rent API and Census ACS 5-Year API to build a county-level dataset (all 50 states + territories) of 2-bedroom FMR and vacancy rates, then runs OLS in R with stargazer tables. No standalone CSV committed -- the pulled table lives inside notebook cell output only.
candidates.why_useful: Working, documented calls against the HUD FMR API and ACS API for full county coverage; could be adapted to rebuild a county-level FMR/ACS-rent time series matched to Airbnb long-term-rental substitution analysis, but requires re-running the notebook to get real data out.
candidates.time_coverage: current HUD FMR + ACS 5-Year vintage at time of run
candidates.size_hint: one ~95KB notebook, no separate data files

candidates.name: Analysis-using-HUD-Fair-Market-Rent-Data
candidates.what_it_holds: Described as a 'lakehouse' analytics project over HUD FMR benchmarks with 'clean, interpretable datasets and visual summaries of how rents vary by geography and unit type'; not directory-inspected (budget), so committed-data status unconfirmed from description alone.
candidates.why_useful: If the lakehouse tables are actually committed (parquet/CSV under a data/ folder), this would be a ready-made structured HUD FMR panel by geography and unit type (studio/1BR/2BR/3BR/4BR), which is the standard proxy for long-term rent floors that compete with Airbnb's monthly-stay segment.
candidates.geography: US, HUD FMR geography (metro/county FMR areas)

candidates.name: fmr-map
candidates.what_it_holds: Interactive choropleth map of HUD Fair Market Rent by geography (small hobby repo, 0 stars, last updated Aug 2026); likely bundles a processed HUD FMR GeoJSON/CSV to drive the map but not directory-confirmed.
candidates.why_useful: A small, recent, actively-touched HUD FMR visualization -- if it bundles a static FMR-by-county file for the map, that's a ready join key set (FIPS/FMR area codes) we could reuse instead of re-deriving HUD's own area definitions.

candidates.name: Zoning-and-Rent-Burdens
candidates.what_it_holds: Academic-style analysis combining Census ACS data, TIGER/Line Shapefiles, HUD Fair Market Rents, and the Wharton Residential Land Use Regulatory Index (WRLURI) to study how metro zoning stringency affects rent burden.
candidates.why_useful: WRLURI + ACS rent-burden combination is a genuinely distinct angle (housing-supply elasticity by metro) that could help explain why some ABNB markets see faster STR-to-LTR conversion pressure than others; more research-package than raw feed but the WRLURI linkage is uncommon in this space.
candidates.time_coverage: WRLURI vintage (2018 index) + ACS multi-year estimates

candidates.name: Housing_Affordability_Analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis of HUD Fair Market Rents and rent-to-income affordability across U.S. counties; described only, not directory-inspected.
candidates.why_useful: Another county-level HUD FMR + affordability build; marginal unless it commits a clean county panel we can reuse directly.

candidates.name: tidyZillow
candidates.what_it_holds: R package/scripts to 'tidy' Zillow Research data (ZHVI/ZORI-style CSVs) into long/tidy format for analysis; small utility repo, 2 stars.
candidates.why_useful: A reusable tidying utility for Zillow's own published research CSVs (which we can download directly from Zillow's research page) -- saves reshape work if we pull ZORI/ZHVI ourselves, but adds no new data.
candidates.time_coverage: whatever Zillow Research vintage is fed in
candidates.size_hint: small R utility, no data committed

candidates.name: us-housing-buy-vs-rent
candidates.what_it_holds: R/Shiny interactive app comparing buy-vs-rent cost across US metros using Zillow research data (ZHVI for prices, presumably ZORI for rent); MIT licensed, updated Aug 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Working, recently-touched Shiny app pulling Zillow buy-vs-rent metro series; the buy/rent cost gap is a plausible macro driver of household formation and short-vs-long-term rental substitution, but the repo is a live app over Zillow's own feed, not a static dataset.
candidates.size_hint: no data committed, live Shiny pulls

candidates.name: hud-fair-market-rents-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: An Apify actor (cloud scraper-as-a-service wrapper) for pulling HUD Fair Market Rent data; requires an Apify account/run to get output, no data committed to the repo.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal -- just a thin Apify wrapper around HUD's own public FMR data/API, which we could query directly for free without needing Apify.
candidates.size_hint: no data committed, Apify actor config only

notes: This theme is heavily saturated with one-off student/bootcamp notebooks that call the Zillow Research CSV downloads, the HUD Fair Market Rent API, and the Census ACS API live and commit no data of their own -- confirmed by directory-listing three of the more promising-looking ones (redfin-market-pulse, Housing-Market-Data-Analysis, ETL-Housing-Pipeline): all gitignore their data output. No genuine Apartment List rent-estimate mirror or scraper surfaced in 'apartment list rent estimates' or 'apartment list rent' searches -- Apartment List does not appear to have a notable open-source GitHub presence for its rent-estimate research series; if this gap matters, the direct path is Apartment List's own public CSV downloads on apartmentlist.com/research, not GitHub. No Realtor.com rental-data repos or CoStar-adjacent open repos turned up at all in six searches. Best remaining leads (medium potential, not directory-confirmed due to gh-search-call budget): josephowadee/Analysis-using-HUD-Fair-Market-Rent-Data (claims a 'lakehouse' of clean HUD FMR datasets by geography and unit type) and Asyed723/Zoning-and-Rent-Burdens (ACS + TIGER + HUD FMR + WRLURI zoning-stringency index, a genuinely distinct join not seen elsewhere in this sweep) -- worth a follow-up WebFetch on their README/contents if another scout has budget. Note: this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200 used by other work) before I could cross-check with plain web search, so coverage here relies solely on `gh search repos` (6 calls, budget-exhausted) plus 3 `gh api contents` spot checks; a rerun with WebSearch available might surface a real Zillow ZORI/ZHVI Python package (e.g. a PyPI-published wrapper) or an Apartment List GitHub org that this pass missed.
